Surah 107, verses 1–7

Makkan; it has one hundred and twenty-five letters, twenty-five words, and seven verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Faqih informed me, saying: Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hamid told us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Isfahani told us, saying: Mu'mil ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri told us, saying:

Aslam al-Minqari told us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah Ara'aita, Allah will forgive him if he is one who pays zakat." [268] [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/454.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?﴾ Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning al-‘As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi. Al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Ibn Kaysan said: It means al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. Al-Dahhak said: It concerns Amr ibn A'idh ibn Imran ibn Makhzum; it was also said: Hubayra ibn Abi Wahb al-Makhzumi. Ibn Jurayj said: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb used to slaughter two camels every week, and an orphan came to him asking for something, so he struck him with his staff. Then Allah the Exalted revealed concerning him: ﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? That is the one who repulses the orphan﴾, that is, he oppresses him, drives him away and pushes him back from his right. Al-Da‘‘: pushing with harshness.

Abu Raja' recited ﴿yada‘u﴾ (he leaves) the orphan, meaning he abandons him and falls short in his rights. ﴿And does not urge the feeding of the needy.﴾ ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer.﴾

Abdullah ibn Hamid told us, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sa'ali in Baghdad told us, saying: Amr ibn al-Rabi' ibn Tariq told us, saying: Ikrimah ibn Ibrahim told us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about His saying: ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾. Ibn Abbas said: They are the hypocrites, who abandon the prayer in private when people are absent, and perform it in public when they are present.

Its explanation is His saying: ﴿And when they stand up to pray, they stand lazily, showing off to the people﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 142], etc. Mujahid said: They are distracted and unmindful of it, treating it with negligence. Qatadah said: "Heedless of it" means one who does not care whether he prayed or did not pray.

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj told them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Hisham told us, from Shaybān al-Nahwi, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: A man told me, from Abu Burda al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said when this verse was revealed, ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾: "Allahu Akbar! This is better for you than if each one of you were given the whole of the world. It is one who, if he prays, does not hope for the good of his prayer, and if he abandons it, does not fear his Lord." [269] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/404.]

And with the same chain from Ibn Jarir, who said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, saying: Amr ibn Abi Maslama told us, saying: I heard Umar ibn Sulayman narrate from Ata' ibn Dinar that he said: Praise be to Allah who said ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾ and did not say "in their prayer." Al-Hasan said: It is one who, if he prays, prays for show, and if it is missed, does not regret it. Abu al-‘Aliyah said: They do not pray at its appointed times, nor do they complete its bowing or its prostrations. From him also: It is one who, when he prostrates, moves his head this way and that, turning his face. Al-Dahhak said: They are those who abandon the prayer.

﴿And withhold the small kindnesses (al-ma'un).﴾

Abu Bakr al-Jamshadi told us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Qati'i told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Muslim told us, saying: Abu Amr al-Darir told us, saying: Abu Awana told us, from Isma'il al-Sahmi, from Abu Salih, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), concerning ﴿al-ma'un﴾, that he said: It is zakat.

This was also the view of Ibn Umar, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn al-Hanafiyya and al-Dahhak.

Al-Jamshadi also informed us, saying: Al-‘Utayfi informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Muslim told us, saying: Abu Amr al-Darir told us, saying: Hammad told us, from ‘Asim, from Zirr, from Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), concerning al-ma'un, that he said: The axe, the bucket, the cooking pot and similar things. This is also the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid reported from him: it is the loan of items and household goods. Ata' reported from him: it is obedience. Muhammad ibn Ka'b and al-Kalbi said: al-Ma'un is all that is well known, which people exchange among themselves. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Zuhri and Muqatil said: al-Ma'un is wealth, in the dialect of Quraysh. Al-A'sha said:

"With what is better than his al-ma'un, when their sky is not overcast."

Muhammad ibn Abdus informed us, along with others, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm told us, saying: al-Farra' told us, saying: I heard some of the Arabs say: al-Ma'un is water, and he recited to me in this regard: "It spills the cup of al-ma'un, pouring." Al-Sabir is the sour milk.

Abu Ubayd and al-Mubarrad said: In the Jahiliyya, al-ma'un was every benefit, gift and loan; in Islam it is obedience and zakat. Hassan ibn Qahhaf said: "He does not deprive the one who seeks his al-ma'un." The Arabs also say: "We alighted, so you made for us a favour with your she-camel, giving you al-ma'un," meaning obedience and submission. The poet said:

"When he strives against them with the reins, they submit or give al-ma'un."

Al-Farra' also related from some of them that they said: al-ma'un is from al-ma'in (flowing water). Qutrub said: The root of al-ma'un is scarcity; the Arabs say: "He has neither sa'na nor ma'na," meaning nothing little. So they called zakat, charity and kindness al-ma'un, because it is a little from much. It was also said: al-ma'un is what it is not lawful to withhold, such as water, salt and fire. This is supported by what:

Ibn Fanjawayh told us, saying: Amr ibn Mirdas told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, saying: Uthman ibn Mutar told us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from A'isha, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is it that it is not lawful to withhold?" He said: "Water, salt and fire." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is water, but what about fire and salt?" He said to her: "O Humayra, whoever gives fire, it is as if he has given in charity all that was cooked with that fire; whoever gives salt, it is as if he has given in charity all that was seasoned with that salt; whoever gives a drink of water where water is found, it is as if he has freed sixty souls; and whoever gives a drink of water where water is not found, it is as if he has revived a soul." [270] [Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/826.]

The poet al-Ra'i said:

"A people upon Islam, who do not withhold their al-ma'un, nor withhold the tahlil."

Ibn Fanjawayh told us, saying: Amr ibn Mirdas told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, saying: Uthman ibn Mutar told us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from A'isha, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is it that it is not lawful to withhold?" He said: "Water, salt and fire." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is water, but what about fire and salt?" He said to her: "O Humayra, whoever gives fire, it is as if he has given in charity all that was cooked with that fire; whoever gives salt, it is as if he has given in charity all that was seasoned with that salt; whoever gives a drink of water where water is found, it is as if he has freed sixty souls; and whoever gives a drink of water where water is not found, it is as if he has revived a soul." [270] [Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/826.]

The poet al-Ra'i said:

"A people upon Islam, who do not withhold their al-ma'un, nor withhold the tahlil."
